chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Purification of the Four Fundamental Faculties

---

**¶2:** The four fundamental faculties of the spiritual mind — love, wisdom, truth, and perception — [GAP-1: REVIEW are what is] undergoing regeneration. From their origin in the Divine they are holy, alive with spiritual life, and illuminating with heavenly light. However, when they entered into [GAP-2: …] the first spiritual combat of temptation, the corruption of evil was [GAP-3: REVIEW intermingled] with them, and the falsity that proceeds from hell became conjoined with them. And when these faculties descended into the external natural mind, putting off the corrupted external truths that had clothed them, they deposited those corruptions in the selfhood, the proprium. The falsities and evils that they have cast off shall be made manifest in a [GAP-4: …] and become a source of destruction to the external natural mind.

**¶3:** The corruption that love turned to self-love disgorges and deposits in the natural mind is the profaned life-force of perverted vitality. The emanation of that perverted vitality is the burning of wrath. The emanation of wrath is the disordered flowing states of the unregenerate mind.

**¶4:** Likewise, the corruptions that perverted truths discharge from themselves are the concupiscences of disordered desire. The emanation of concupiscence is interior anguish and bitterness. The emanation of bitterness is the inflamed restlessness that consumes the natural mind.

**¶5:** The corruption that wisdom in its fallen state disgorges is the selfhood — the proprium. The emanation of the proprium is spiritual obscurity and darkness of understanding. [GAP-5: REVIEW The] emanation of that spiritual obscurity is hardened resistance against all divine influx — obstinacy of will.

**¶6:** The corruptions that perception in its fallen state disgorges are the false persuasions arising from the pride of self-derived intelligence — the empty声 声ounds of vain reasoning rooted in shame before the Divine. The emanation of those false persuasions from self-intelligence [GAP-6: is …]

**¶7:** The emanation of [GAP-7: REVIEW the grief of spiritual anguish] is the [GAP-8: …] completion and summation of these twelve corruptions flowing from the four faculties — three emanations proceeding from each, forming the full system of spiritual disorder in the unregenerate mind.

**¶8:** [GAP-9: …] these four fundamental faculties shall [GAP-10: …] what is gathered inward is [f]ound through the providential ordering of the spiritual nourishment from the Word [GAP-11: REVIEW that] enters the external natural mind. When the goods and truths of that nourishment enter the natural mind, the faculties are purified and reformed and regenerated, and they are established in their true living spiritual form, which is the new person — the regenerated human being. They come alive [GAP-12: …] and receive the Divine Wisdom flowing into the understanding and the will, and they are purified in their original heavenly form; and they come forth from the natural mind, being cleansed and made holy. They attain their first state of heavenly peace and rest.

**¶9:** They are purified and ascend into heaven, the state of the truly living; but those who come to [GAP-13: …] and pass through those states and [GAP-14: … / …] remaining in falsities and evils. Their end shall be a continual cycling through states of vastation, wandering without rest in the spiritual world.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [the mingling] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [form] and become a danger to the body.
The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is sorrow. The emission of sorrow is the tear]
The emission of the [tear] is the [last] of these twelve emissions.

[Now] these four elements shall [disgorge, and] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [again] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.

they shall be cleansed and go u[p to] the land of the living ones; but these that come to [the flesh] and pass through them and [ ... / ... ] in sins. Their end will occur in transmigration and spirit.

fills.explanation: The editor's phrase "are what is" correctly introduces the four elements as the subject undergoing purification, matching the spiritual sense of the four faculties being regenerated.

In Manichaean cosmogony the light elements entered into "the mingling" (mixture with darkness) in the first battle; this directly anticipates the next clause — "the waste was mixed in with them, and the darkness of the enemy was mixed with them."

The editor's "mixed" is confirmed — "the waste was mixed in with them" is the natural-plane expression for the intermingling of evil with the faculties during the first combat, and "mixed" is the standard Kephalaia term for this cosmological event.

The stripped-off pollutions become manifest in a "form" — the standard Kephalaia term for corruption taking visible shape in the body, corresponding to the twelve emissions described in the following paragraphs.
The editor's "The" is confirmed as the article beginning the parallel clause "The emission of gloom is obstinacy," matching the pattern established in ¶3 and ¶4.

fills.fill: is sorrow. The emission of sorrow is the tear
fills.explanation: The three-per-element pattern requires an intermediate emission between winds of shame and tear to reach twelve total; sorrow is the natural bridge from shame to tears, corresponding to the spiritual grief that proceeds from false persuasions of self-intelligence.

The editor's "tear" is confirmed — it is the natural-plane expression for the grief of spiritual anguish, and as the 12th and final emission it completes the set of three emanations from the tree element.

The tear, as the twelfth emission completing the four three-fold chains, is declared "the last of these twelve emissions" — a summation statement closing the enumeration before the purification process begins in ¶8.

A discourse marker transitioning from the enumeration of twelve emissions (¶3–7) to the purification process (¶8); "Now" is the standard Kephalaia transitional particle for shifting to a new phase of exposition.

The chapter's dominant verb "disgorge" (used in ¶3–6 for each element) governs this clause: the four elements shall disgorge their pollutions, and what remains gathered within is then found and nourished by the soul food.
The editor's "that" is confirmed as the relative pronoun connecting "soul food" to "enters the body," matching the spiritual sense of divine nourishment from the Word entering the natural mind.

After being established in the living image of the new man, the purified elements "live again" — the natural-plane expression for regeneration, the restoration of spiritual life after the disgorging of corruption.

Contrasting with those who ascend to "the land of the living ones," those who fail purification come to "the flesh" — the unregenerate bodily state — and pass through incarnations without being cleansed, ending in transmigration.
